title: Boğaziçi Food Operations Deep Dive

decision_thesis.current_hypothesis: A human-reviewed production/allocation decision may be improved if aggregate demand signals are available before the quantity freeze deadline.
decision_thesis.highest_value_unknown: Who controls final production/allocation quantity, when it is frozen, what signals are available before that deadline, and what the operational cost of excess versus shortage is.

facts.claim: The 2025 SKS activity report lists six dining halls, 6,000 daily meals, packaged-meal service, 2,386 satisfaction-survey participants, a virtual-card system, a North Campus kiosk, a two-year meal tender, and BUCampus menu selection.
caveats: The denominator/period for the source's '2,000 packaged meals' value is not sufficiently defined for reuse as a quantitative model field.

facts.claim: The Food Services Branch Directorate formally prepares tender work and technical specifications, monitors contractor food service, handles meal-pricing processes, prepares/publishes menus, checks contract compliance, and serves the Food Services Executive Board.
caveats: The directive does not identify who chooses production quantity or when the quantity is locked.

facts.claim: Food preparation, distribution and post-distribution cleaning are supplied through a contracted service under university monitoring/control structures.
caveats: Payment basis, waste incentives, shortage penalties and quantity discretion are not established publicly.

facts.claim: BUCampus supports a weekly Wednesday-lunch menu vote with institutional identity and displays survey results; packaged menus and academic/event calendars are also exposed through the app ecosystem.
caveats: Menu preference votes are not attendance reservations or served-demand labels.

facts.claim: Dining support workflows reference date, time, campus and turnstile information for BUCard incidents, and BUCampus QR can be used at dining turnstiles; aggregate dining-entry data are therefore a high-value data-access question.
caveats: No public evidence establishes retention, exportability, team access, one-to-one meal semantics, or a unified QR/BUCard history.

facts.claim: Summer and campus-specific announcements materially change which meal services are available, creating structural service-regime changes that must be separated from low demand.
Public dining pages expose menu context by date/meal/channel and can include kcal and cooked portion gram weights.
caveats: Public availability does not itself authorize unrestricted production scraping; terms and project policy must be respected.

facts.claim: The 2024 SKS report lists 157,697 student breakfasts, 1,157,911 student meals and 96,838 staff meals, totaling 1,412,446 reported servings across those categories.
caveats: These are 2024 annual serving counts and must not be conflated with 2025 daily-meal or beneficiary figures.

facts.claim: The 2025 SKS report lists 1,091 meal-scholarship recipients and describes direct/in-kind meal support.
caveats: Personally identifying scholarship status should not be used as a model input; only privacy-safe aggregate effects should be considered if operationally necessary and authorized.

source_conflicts.rule: Preserve both with source/year metadata; do not impose either as a hard pilot capacity constraint without owner confirmation.
Do not derive participation ratios across differently defined audience/beneficiary metrics.
Do not calculate monthly recycling rates until generation-date versus collection-date semantics are resolved.
Keep period/denominator UNKNOWN until Food Services confirms the published metric definition.

candidate_data_sources.public_clue: BUCard/QR dining turnstiles with date/time/campus/turnstile support metadata
weekly BUCampus Wednesday lunch menu survey
central kitchen and contracted preparation/distribution operation
academic calendar plus dining service-change announcements

model_rules: Start with interpretable decision-compatible baselines before complex temporal models.
Use time-aware evaluation; do not use random row-wise train/test splitting for deployment claims.
Add calendar/service-regime, menu, poll and other context by ablation.
Evaluate excess and shortage/service-level consequences in addition to forecast accuracy.
Derive asymmetric excess-versus-shortage costs from operator evidence, not arbitrary coefficients.
Do not use university-level monthly food-waste totals as a production recommendation target.
Treat policy heuristic bands separately from calibrated uncertainty.
Include current operator forecasting as a baseline when it can be prospectively recorded.

minimum_pilot_export.privacy_rule: Request aggregate operational data; do not require personal identifiers.

research_hypotheses.hypothesis: Food Services Branch is a key administrative decision stakeholder.
Aggregate BUCard/QR entry data can provide a historical served-demand proxy.
BUCampus menu votes contain predictive information beyond menu identity.
Service-regime flags materially improve forecast robustness.
Contractor incentives allow lower production recommendations to create economic value.
Production can be adjusted in multiple batches after partial demand is observed.
Packaged meals are a separate demand channel requiring separate forecasting/allocation.

IE: Interview Food Services Branch before generic student discovery for the production-decision workflow.
Resolve contractor payment/incentive structure and quantity authority.
Use last-incident questions to establish freeze time, shortage consequences and excess consequences.
EE: Map planned→produced→served→surplus→waste measurement boundaries and existing systems of record.
Prefer existing logs and manual audited measurements before proposing new hardware.
CS1: Benchmark service-regime-aware baselines before complex models.
Treat BUCard/QR aggregates as a candidate served-demand proxy only after reconciliation.
Test menu votes/menu identity/calendar features by time-aware ablation.
Optimize decision cost under shortage guardrails, not MAE alone.
CS2: Use governance and service-scale facts as public-source context, not PMR validation.
Frame the unresolved problem around production/allocation timing and existing aggregate signals.
Do not claim data access, causality or achieved savings before interviews/pilot evidence.
